# opencode-smart-ui Rich chat UI for the opencode desktop chat: SVG charts, colored text blocks, structured panels, native question menus and graded quizzes — rendered in the conversation, not as raw JSON. Two engines ship in one package: - **V2 (opencode desktop 2.2.5+)** — the model writes charts as ordinary reply text: a hidden `` spec followed by an image link. The plugin renders the SVG while the message streams, so charts cost **zero tool calls**. Panels are written as plain markdown/HTML. `smartui_show` remains a fallback (and the only path on the `art` surface); menus and quizzes relay the built-in `question` tool. - **V1 (opencode 1.18.29+)** — the model writes `smartui-show` / `smartui-form` fences and the plugin patches the text parts in place. Includes embedded HTML forms and a local chart server. ## Install ### V2 (desktop 2.2.5+) Use the `plugins` key: ```jsonc // ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc (global) or .opencode/opencode.jsonc (project) { "plugins": ["opencode-smart-ui"] } ``` Pass options with the object form: ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "opencode-smart-ui", "options": { "surface": "image", "injectPrompt": true, "coloredText": true } } ] } ``` A local checkout must point at the package **directory**, not at `src/index.ts`: ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "C:/projects/plugin/opencode_plugin", "options": { "surface": "image" } } ] } ``` ### V1 (legacy) Use the legacy `plugin` key. A package name works, or a `[path, options]` tuple for a local file: ```jsonc { "plugin": [ ["C:/projects/plugin/opencode_plugin/src/index.ts", { "surface": "image", "injectPrompt": true }] ] } ``` ## Visual blocks (V2) Charts are ordinary reply text — **no tool call**. For every chart write exactly two lines, one after the other: ```markdown ![Builds](file:///C:/Users/you/AppData/Local/opencode-smartui/charts/buildswk42.svg) ``` - Line 1 is an HTML comment: it carries the spec and stays invisible in the chat. - Line 2 is the image the user sees. The plugin renders the spec to that exact `.svg` path while the message streams, before the link appears. - `key` is 4–32 lowercase letters/digits and unique per chart in the conversation — a short name plus a random suffix, such as `buildswk42`. The key in the comment and the file name must match exactly. - Never wrap either line in a code fence, never indent it, and don't describe the syntax around it. - Only charts use this flow. Panels are written directly (see below). Panels — plain markdown/HTML, no tool call: | Panel | How to write it | |---|---| | table | a markdown table | | stats | a markdown table of label/value metrics with a delta and ▲/▼/— trend | | kv | a two-column label/value table with the label bold | | badges | inline code chips joined with ` · ` | | checklist | a GFM task list (`- [x]` / `- [ ]`), optional `**Progress: 62%**` | | callout | a blockquote with a bold lead: `> **Warning** — text` | | quote | `> text` plus `> — Author` on its own line | | banner | one key takeaway; see below | ### Fallback tool `smartui_show` still exists for the `art` surface and for clients that cannot render local images. On the image surface the two-line flow is preferred; call the tool only when the user explicitly asks for exact tool rendering. It returns a `DISPLAY` block between `----- BEGIN DISPLAY -----` and `----- END DISPLAY -----`; copy the content between the markers into the reply verbatim, as plain markdown on its own paragraph. Never print the markers themselves. Elements — pick by data shape: | Data shape | Elements | |---|---| | `data: [{label, value}]` | `bar`, `donut`, `waterfall`, `funnel`, `treemap` | | `labels` + `series` | `column` (add `stacked` / `percent`), `line`, `area`, `radar` | | `values: [...]` | `sparkline` | | `series: [{name, points}]` | `scatter` (optional `alpha`, `radius`) | | `matrix` | `heatmap` (optional `rowLabels`, `columnLabels`) | | `spans` | `timeline` (`dates: true` for epoch ms) | | `value` | `gauge`, `progress` (optional `min`, `max`, `bands`) | | `items` | `stats`, `kv`, `checklist`, `badges` | | `columns` + `rows` / text | `table`, `callout`, `quote` | | `title` + `subtitle` | `banner` (optional `tone`) | Shared keys: `title`, `subtitle`, `unit`; charts also accept `height`. ### Colored text blocks In V2 a `banner` is inline HTML written straight into the reply — a heading line and a subtext line, each with its own background: ```html
Release 0.2.4
Colored text blocks are live.
``` Tone palettes (border / heading bg / subtext bg; text stays near-white): blue `#33507a` / `#16324d` / `#292348` · violet `#4b3a72` / `#32204d` / `#1d2f4d` · teal `#2b5f63` / `#0f383c` / `#1b3040` · amber `#6b5124` / `#3b2a0d` / `#3a2114` · rose `#71384b` / `#401923` / `#331b33` · slate `#3f444d` / `#23262c` / `#2c3038`. The block is real HTML with inline styles, so the text stays selectable, wraps naturally and keeps the chat font. Set `coloredText` to `false` to have the prompt ask for a plain bold heading and paragraph instead. The same banner is available through `smartui_show` / `smartui-show` with `{ "element": "banner", "title": "…", "subtitle": "…", "tone": "blue" }`. ### Data input - **Inline JSON** — the full shape, e.g. `"series":[{"name":"North","values":[12,15,9]}]`. - **Compact shorthand** — `"labels":"Q1,Q2,Q3"`, `"values":"1 2 3"`, `"data":"A:3, B:7"`, `"spans":"design:0:4; build:3:9"`. - **`source`** — `"source":"reports/revenue.csv"` (`.csv`, `.tsv` or `.json`, resolved against the project directory then the workspace root, 2 MB / 2000-row cap — scatter is allowed 16 MB / 300k rows and is sampled to 20k dots, or an absolute path). The element then names its columns instead of holding the numbers: bar/donut/waterfall/funnel/treemap use `"label"`+`"value"`; column/line/area/radar use `"labels"`+`"series"`; scatter uses `"x"`+`"y"` (+ optional `"group"`); heatmap uses `"row"`+`"column"`+`"value"`; timeline uses `"label"`+`"start"`+`"end"`; progress uses `"value"`. Column refs may be a column name or a 0-based index. Generate the file with your own tools first — nothing executes inside a block. ## Menus and quizzes (V2) | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `smartui_ask` | Ask the user — a menu or free-text question whose answer decides what happens next. Returns an inline card plus an action telling the model to call the built-in `question` tool with the same questions. With `inline: true` the card is the whole interaction: no dock, the user answers in chat. | | `smartui_quiz` | Stateful questionnaire: server-side answer keys, batch or one-question-at-a-time, grading with explanations and a summary table. Supports multiple-choice and fill-in questions (`answer` alternates separated by `|`). | For structured input with several fields, use the built-in `question` tool directly (or `smartui_ask` with `purpose: "form"`, which writes an inline card and then relays the same questions to the dock). V2 has no HTML form surface; the V1 `smartui-form` fence is not processed by the V2 plugin. ## Visual blocks (V1) Charts, panels and forms are plain fenced JSON blocks the model writes straight into its reply — no tool call. When the assistant message completes the plugin parses each fence and patches the text part in place: ````markdown ```smartui-show {"element":"column","title":"Builds","labels":["Mon","Tue"],"series":[{"values":[3,7]}]} ``` ```smartui-form {"title":"Launch survey","questions":[{"header":"Name","question":"What is your name?"}]} ``` ```` - `smartui-show` — the same elements and data input as V2. Charts are SVG images served by a local server; on the `art` surface (or when the server is down) they degrade to unicode art in a code fence. Panels are plain markdown. - `smartui-form` — a real HTML form (text, textarea, radio, checkbox, select — up to 8 questions). The user fills it in place and presses Send; answers arrive automatically as a new user message and the form region swaps to a "✓ submitted" receipt card. A malformed block becomes a one-line error note instead of failing the turn. - `smartui_form` — collect-only recovery tool that fetches a pending form's answers by `key` if the automatic submission did not arrive. ### V1 form capture - **In-app log bridge (default).** The form's `action` is `xmpp://` with `target="_blank"`. The desktop sanitizer keeps `xmpp:` but the external-URL policy blocks it; the blocked submission is written to the app's log, which the plugin tails and turns into a user message. No browser tab and no navigation. - **HTTP fallback.** If the log directory can't be resolved, the form posts to the plugin's local server (`/f//`) and a brief confirmation tab completes the flow. Force either with `SMARTUI_FORM_TRANSPORT=log|http`; override the logs root with `SMARTUI_FORM_LOG_ROOT`. ## Options Plugin options (V2 `options` object or V1 tuple second element): ```jsonc { "surface": "image", "injectPrompt": true, "coloredText": true } ``` - `surface` — `"image"` (default) renders charts as SVG; `"art"` emits compact unicode art in a code fence. If the chart file cannot be written, charts fall back to art automatically. - `injectPrompt` — set `false` to skip the system-prompt guidance. - `coloredText` — default `true`. Set `false` to render `banner` blocks as plain markdown (bold heading plus paragraph) instead of colored HTML. ## How rendering works **V2.** Charts are written as hidden `` comments in the assistant text. The plugin subscribes to `session.text.delta` / `session.text.ended`, renders each complete spec to `/charts/.svg` as the message streams, and dedupes repeated renders (including a spec split across deltas). The markdown image link that follows resolves the local SVG; the desktop inlines it as a data URI. No HTTP server is started. Local SVGs are pruned after 7 days, with a 512-file cap. The system prompt is injected with the `session.hook("context")` extension point, so the chart base path matches the data directory on that machine. `smartui_show` renders the same payload on the `art` surface or when explicitly requested. **V1.** `opencode` v1 does not render custom tool output, so everything visible is delivered through server-side patches of the assistant's text parts: 1. The model writes `smartui-show` / `smartui-form` fences as ordinary reply text. 2. On `message.part.updated` the plugin stashes parts that contain a fence; when the message completes (or the session goes idle) it re-fetches the final part text, parses the fences and patches the part once: - shows are replaced by the rendered payload (chart `` markdown or panel markdown) directly; - forms are replaced by marker-wrapped HTML (` … `) and the card is registered and bound, so the later submitted-receipt swap can find the region again. 3. Image charts point at the plugin's local chart server (`http://127.0.0.1:/c//.svg`), which serves the SVG for 6h. Chart SVGs and the server identity (token + port) are persisted to disk so chart images in past messages keep loading after an app restart; expired files are pruned on the same 6h TTL. Form records are persisted the same way (`forms/`, one small JSON per form), so form cards in past messages can still be submitted and the receipt swap still works. Writes are best-effort, reads are lazy, and the same 6h TTL plus a 256-record cap keeps disk use bounded. The question dock and quiz relay the built-in `question` tool — the question card is written into the chat first (INLINE CARD), so the questions render inline above the dock while the user answers. With `inline: true` (chat mode) there is no dock at all: the card carries a "Reply in chat" hint and the user answers by typing. `smartui-form` embeds **real HTML** (`
`), which the desktop renderer passes through sanitized (DOMPurify keeps `form`/`input`/`select`/`button`, strips scripts, and prefixes `id`/`name` with `user-content-`). ## Data directory Chart SVGs (and V1 form records / server identity) live under: - Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\opencode-smartui` - macOS/Linux: `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode-smartui` or `~/.local/share/opencode-smartui` - Override: `SMARTUI_DATA_DIR` ## Dev ```powershell npm install npm run typecheck # tsc --noEmit npm test # node --test (Node >= 22, uses type stripping) ``` Set `SMARTUI_DEBUG=1` to log bridge activity to `%TEMP%\smartui-debug.log`. ## Layout ``` src/ index.ts dual entry: V2 default export + V1 server plugin v2-plugin.ts V2 Plugin.define, tool schemas, file chart publisher v2-render.ts hidden-comment extraction + streamed chart rendering block-core.ts V1 fence scanning/parsing, block rendering, one-shot patch bridge.ts V1 marker protocol: bind on part events, patch, message injection show-core.ts chart/panel rendering (element registry, hydration, source loading) banner.ts colored heading/subtext HTML block + plain-markdown fallback data-source.ts CSV/TSV/JSON dataset loading + column helpers server.ts V1 local chart + form server (persisted port + token paths) chart-store.ts on-disk chart SVG + server identity persistence form-store.ts on-disk form record persistence + memory-first reload dock.ts question-dock JSON relay quiz-core.ts question normalization, grading, card rendering form-core.ts form normalization, HTML rendering, receipt, query capture log-transport.ts V1 electron-log tailing (blocked-target capture) state.ts in-memory quiz + form store (6h TTL, 32/session) options.ts plugin options prompts.ts V1 and V2 injected prompts / tool descriptions tools/ ask.ts, quiz.ts, form.ts (collect-only) svg/ core.ts, charts.ts, panels.ts, payload.ts art/ fallback.ts (unicode charts) test/ node:test suites ```
